ud_dawn_skitterers.accept_text:
Clear them off the shelf. I have lost two sighting glasses this month and the Codex's position is that I should be more careful with Codex property.

They are not aggressive so much as curious, which makes no difference to the glass. Work the scree at the shelf edge - that is where they nest, and they do not go far from it.

ud_sporefall_caps.accept_text:
Caps off the grazers out in the forest proper, not the little ones at the rim. The rim stock is stunted and the Codex's cooks can taste the difference, which I resent.

The ones that look like faces are fine, incidentally. Everybody asks. The stalks will put you on the floor for a day, so leave the stalks.
ud_sporefall_caps.turn_in_text:
All of them, and two of them good enough to argue about.

You are not from here either, are you. Nor am I, in the sense that matters. Everyone in this cavern walked in, which is the only thing I like about it.

ud_sporefall_drifters.accept_text:
All of them, and thin them out along the paths between the big caps - that is where they drift and that is where the foragers walk.

Mind the ones that are already clustered. They share something between them, and the second you start on one the rest of the cloud is stronger for it. Break them up before they can close ranks, or you will fight the whole grove at once.

ud_shard_crates.accept_text:
Cores, and take them out of the lattice sentries rather than off the ground. Ground stock is half shell and the Reagent-Keeper sends it back with a note.

The sentries will let you walk out there. They object when you start cutting. There is no way to do this politely and I have stopped looking for one.
ud_shard_crates.turn_in_text:
Weighed, and I will weigh them again at the gate.

If they come out lighter up there, it is not you. It has been happening for a year and the Codex's explanation is the scales.

ud_silver_bars.accept_text:
Bars. Dig it out of the fields yourself and smelt it yourself - I am not sending ore up to the Bastion so that a factor can take a cut of my own rock.

There is silver all through this plain. There is also iron, and coal in thin seams, so you will not be short of a fire. Bring me bars and I will put your name in the ledger as a field hand, which is worth more down here than it sounds.
ud_silver_bars.turn_in_text: All of them, and clean. You will find most people down here can do one half of a trade. The Codex trains specialists and then puts them two hundred spans from anybody else's specialty.

ud_lattice_repeats.accept_text:
Sentries, and I want them taken apart rather than simply dropped. Cut them where the figure closes - you will see it, there is a seam in the pattern and it is always in the same place relative to the body.

If it is always in the same place on all of them, that is not mineralisation. That is a design, and designs have designers, and I will put THAT in a report whatever the Codex rules.
ud_lattice_repeats.turn_in_text:
All of them. Same seam, same offset, to within a finger's width.

I am going to write the word 'manufactured' and I am going to sign it, and then I expect I will be having a conversation with the Codex-Master.

ud_lattice_measure.accept_text:
The far side of the field, past the standing figures, where the growth is oldest. Cores from there, and the position - I need to know where you stood, not just what you brought back.

Take the long way round the central mass. Going through it is quicker and the sentries in there are thicker than anywhere else in the cavern, and I would rather have the reading late than not at all.

ud_reach_husks.accept_text:
Out in the Reach where the threads run thickest. I will tell you plainly what I think you are doing, because you will work it out yourself and I would rather you heard it here: those were people, or they were something that walked.

The growth did not kill them for food. It kept the shape. It kept the shape and put itself inside it, and I do not have a word for what that is called when a plant does it.
ud_reach_husks.turn_in_text:
Did any of them still have belongings?

I asked that of the last four people I sent and I have four different answers, which means I am going to have to go and look myself.

ud_marsh_timekeeping.accept_text:
Sacs off the leeches in the shallows. Take them at low lumen, when the water is dim - they hold the light at the point you cut them and I want them caught at the bottom of the cycle.

If nine sacs cut an hour apart all show the same phase, then the cycle is not in the water. It is in whatever the water is reading, and so are we.
ud_marsh_timekeeping.turn_in_text:
Same phase. All of them.

There is a clock in this cavern and none of us built it. Three years we have set our watches by the Lumen and called it convenient.

ud_marsh_glimmerjaw.accept_text:
All of them, and work the deep channels rather than the banks. The bank fish are young and they are not what is taking my markers.

Do not follow the light. The lure sits well forward of the animal, and people who swim toward it meet the rest of it on the way.
ud_marsh_glimmerjaw.turn_in_text:
And my markers?

Then they are not taking the markers for the light. Something out there is taking them because they are MARKERS, and I would very much like to be wrong about that.

ud_colonnade_dalaran.turn_in_text:
All of them, and every one of them cut rather than broken.

The Codex's official position is that the masonry fell. Stone that falls two hundred spans does not land in courses. I have said this at three briefings and I will say it at a fourth.
ud_colonnade_dalaran.accept_text:
Walk the colonnade from the south end to where it stops, and bring me worked fragments off the revenants in it. Off them, specifically - what is on the floor is rubble and what they carry was chosen.

I want you to look at the jointing while you are down there. It is Kirin Tor work. It is Kirin Tor work that was never on the surface, because the surface version of these columns is still standing up there with weather on it, and this one has none.

ud_colonnade_dissidents.accept_text:
I am not going to dress this up for you.

They were colleagues. They went out to the colonnade to settle an argument about the masonry and they settled it in a direction the rest of us did not follow, and what came back was not interested in discussing it. They still wear the crimson. Some of them still carry their field books. I have read two and I wish I had not.

ud_archive_interlopers.accept_text:
Out of the Archive precinct. They are not explorers and they are not looking for anything in particular - they are looking for whatever we have already dug up, which saves them the digging.

They came down a hole in the Alterac foothills for the same reason we did, and I am aware of how that sounds. The difference is that we catalogue what we take. I will not pretend that is a large difference. It is the one I have.
ud_archive_interlopers.turn_in_text:
Good.

We arrived three years ago with no more claim than they have and everybody here knows it. We write things down. It is a thin moral position and I would thank you not to test it.

ud_archive_unissued.turn_in_text:
Slips. Numbers, all ahead of my sequence, and before you ask me whose hand it is - yes. I recognise it.

I am not going to say. Not until I have been down to the Bloom myself, and I have been putting that off for eleven months.

ud_dim_walkers.accept_text:
The Dim-walkers. Take them at the boundary rather than hunting them inward. Inward is how I lost a partner.

They will not cross into the light while you are watching. I have sat out there for whole shifts and they do not cross. Turn your back for the length of a slow count and they are thirty paces nearer, still in the dark, and the dark is in a different place than it was.
ud_dim_walkers.turn_in_text:
Off the line.

It will be quiet for about a week. It always is. Then there will be one standing out there again at the start of a shift, and I will not have seen it arrive.

ud_riftward_unfinished.accept_text:
The Codex has filed them as the Unfinished. Kill them, and I want you to watch what they do rather than simply end them. They cast the same spell twice and get two different results, which is not a mistake on their part. The spell is the same. The world it lands in has not settled.

If you can tell me which half is inconsistent - the caster or the ground - you will have told me more than three years of Codex surveying has.

ud_riftward_geometry.accept_text:
Out to the far edge, and samples of the residue off whatever is standing there. Then come back and tell me how many sides it had.

I am not going to tell you my own figure. If I tell you my figure you will see my figure, and that is precisely the error I am trying to rule out.

ud_archive_deeper.accept_text:
You are in the record now, which is the only reason we are having this conversation.

The lower cut, past the shoring, where the Archive stops being masonry and starts being whatever the masonry was built into. More slips off the revenants down there and your own eyes on the face.

I will tell you what I told the last one: do not read them in there. Bring them up first.
